newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania considers bank privatisation plans - PM.
newsitem.headline: Albania considers bank privatisation plans - PM.

text.p: Albanian Prime Minister Aleksander Meksi said the government will consider plans to privatise two of three state banks by the end of August, the daily Koha Jone reported on Wednesday.
Meksi said the first banks to be privatised would be the National Commercial Bank (NCB), the country's biggest, and the Rural Commercial Bank (RCB).
"The banks' privatisation will be discussed by the government as soon as possible, within August," he told Koha Jone in an interview.
"It is one of the conditions we have agreed to with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank," Meksi, a member of the ruling conservative Democratic Party, said.
The IMF is supervising Albania's privatisation strategy of banks.
The paper said the banks would be privatised by selling shares to foreign and local investors and the general public.

"The mechanism to buy into the banks would be privatisation vouchers and since their price has fallen to 11 percent of the nominal value, the future bank shareholders will buy them very cheaply," the paper said.
The state will continue to retain majority control.
"We will clearly define...the forms of keeping control of these banks for the benefit of the Albanian economy," Meksi added.
Albania set up a two-tier bank system with the Bank of Albania serving as central institution to the National Commercial Bank, the Rural Commercial Bank and the Savings Bank.
The National Commercial Bank is the shareholder of two joint venture banks, the Albanian-Italian Bank with Italy's Banca di Roma, and the Arab-Albanian Islamic Bank.
Albania's central bank has given licences to two Greek banks and a Malaysian investor to set up private banks in the Balkan state.
